short: the order in which the reads and writes of concurrent transactions actually ran.
a schedule whose conflicting pairs are all in the same order as in some serial run. tested with a precedence graph.
one node per transaction, an edge when one's operation conflicts with a later one of the other. a cycle means not serializable.
take locks, then release them, and never take a new one after releasing any. guarantees conflict serializability.
two-phase locking that holds write locks until commit, so nobody reads uncommitted data and aborts never cascade.
how a lock may be shared. postgres has eight for tables, from ACCESS SHARE to ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.
the table of which lock modes can be held on one object at the same time. anything else waits.
a lock on one row, stored in the tuple header (xmax plus infomask bits), not in the lock table.
the view of the lock manager: one row per lock held or waited for, with its locktype, mode and granted flag.
the waiters for one object, first come first served. a new request waits behind any queued request it conflicts with.
the longest a statement may wait for any one lock before it fails with 55P03. off by default.
aka: canceling statement due to lock timeout

short: who waits for whom. a cycle of hard waits is a deadlock; a cycle through a queue position is fixed by reordering.
how long a waiting backend sleeps before it checks for a deadlock itself. 1 s by default. not a limit on waiting.
a lightweight lock on a shared memory structure, shared or exclusive, held for microseconds. a wait event, never in pg_locks.
the shortest lock postgres has: a few instructions, taken by busy-waiting. shows up only as Timeout:SpinDelay.
a buffer's content lock plus no other pins. VACUUM needs it to remove dead tuples from a page.
concurrency control that fixes the serial order by start timestamp and aborts operations that arrive too late.
optimistic concurrency control: run on private copies, validate at the end, abort if something you read changed.
serializable snapshot isolation: snapshot isolation plus tracking of read/write dependencies. postgres's SERIALIZABLE.
a note that a serializable transaction read a tuple, page or relation. it blocks nobody and outlives the commit.
a serializable transaction wrote what another one had read, so the reader must come first. two in a row: 40001.
